title: D2B2b2 decision_payload v1 (one purpose, one tenant)
$comment: Fills the gap declared by docs/governance/consent/d2b2b2-decision-packet.template.json#/digest_contract/decision_payload_schema_version. This is the schema of the object that is JCS-canonicalized (RFC 8785) and SHA-256-digested to produce content_digest. It is a pure documentation/governance artifact: it grants no catalog, evidence_store, writer, runtime, migration, or deploy authority. Reference content: docs/governance/consent/d2b2b2-decision-packet-tarefas-operacionais.md.

opaqueUuid.description: Server-generated opaque identifier. MUST NOT be derived from name, phone, message content, or any civil document (see reference doc section 1.1).

opaqueRefOrNull.description: An opaque, non-reversible reference to a fact or record kept in external custody. Never the fact's raw content (no personal document numbers, no personal contact data, no free text of a conversation).

looksLikeForbiddenIdentityValue.description: Best-effort structural guard against pasting raw Brazilian CPF or E.164 phone numbers into an opaque reference field. Not a substitute for the field-name allowlist below, which is the primary control.

forbiddenIdentityFieldNamePattern.description: Property names matching this pattern are personal identity/signature fields (CPF, RG, civil document, personal phone, personal e-mail, address, bank data, secrets). They are forbidden anywhere in decision_payload; the reference doc (sections 1.1, 4.3, 11.2) requires them to live only in external custody records referenced by opaque IDs.

freeformGovernanceObject.description: Structured governance narrative with server-controlled field names. additionalProperties stays true only for keys that pass the forbidden-identity-field-name guard, so no personal identity/signature key can be smuggled in through a nested object.

populatedGovernanceContent.description: Non-empty governance content. May be a short opaque reference, a longer narrative string, a structured object (see freeformGovernanceObject), or a list of either. Placeholder values such as "pendente"/"desconhecido"/"n/a" are rejected by the human-packet completeness check in backend/tests/test_d2b2b2_decision_packet_docs.py, not by this schema.

optionalGovernanceContent.description: Same shape as populatedGovernanceContent, but null is allowed before materialization/attestation completes a given fact.

childrenAdolescentsUnknownAgeAndGuardian.description: Mirrors minor_protection_contract in the template exactly: same seven keys, same enum. UNCERTAIN keeps catalog_ready and writer_eligible false at the packet level (governance envelope, out of scope for this file).
childrenAdolescentsUnknownAgeAndGuardian.$comment: Required-when-APPLICABLE fields (best_interest_assessment_ref, age_or_guardian_measures, risk_and_impact_assessment_ref, reviewer_record_ref) are enforced by the human-packet completeness check (_minor_decision_is_complete in backend/tests/test_d2b2b2_decision_packet_docs.py), not by this structural schema.

retentionSurfaceEntry.description: One row of the retention-and-disposal matrix (reference doc section 14). Opaque policy reference or short structured rule; never the retained content itself.

controllerIdentityAndInstitutionalContac.description: Institutional (not personal) identity of the controlling church and its monitored institutional contact channel. Section 1.1 of the reference doc also lists platform_operator_identity, privacy_contact, notice_location, transfer_notice_location and controller_authority_ref as materialized facts; the current decision_payload contract (this file's DECISION_PAYLOAD_KEYS-equivalent top level) has no dedicated key for them, so they are out of scope here -- see the divergence note in the accompanying test/report.

controller_legal_name.description: Public institutional denomination of the controlling church, e.g. 'Igreja Exemplo'. Not a person's name.

institutional_contact_channel_ref.description: Opaque reference to the monitored institutional contact channel (never a personal phone/e-mail).

noticeTextsByChannelAndLanguage.description: Notice text bodies keyed by delivery channel then by language tag (e.g. 'whatsapp' -> 'pt-BR' -> exact text). Channel and language keys are server-controlled, not free personal text.

purpose.description: Exactly one purpose per materialized decision_payload (see template.json#/metadata/materialization_cardinality).

package_id.description: Server-generated after binding to a tenant. Never derived from name, phone, message, or civil document (reference doc section 1.1).

package_version.description: Immutable semantic version. The first materialization uses the version approved from the DRAFT_NOT_APPROVED text.

supersedes_content_digest.description: null for the first documented version of this purpose+tenant; otherwise the sha256 content_digest of the payload this version replaces (reference doc section 13.3).

tenant_binding.description: Canonical igreja_id selected and validated server-side. Never accepted from the model, message, or free client field (reference doc section 1.1, section 18.2).

legal_hypothesis_common_data.description: Legal basis for common personal data in this purpose (reference doc section 7). Typically LGPD art. 7, I (consent).

legal_hypothesis_sensitive_data.description: Legal basis for sensitive personal data, including religious conviction (reference doc section 7). Typically LGPD art. 11, I (specific, highlighted consent).

consent_based_operation.description: True marks this purpose's design as consent-based (reference doc section 1, metadata table). It never means a person actually granted consent; that fact lives only in the ledger/evidence_store described in section 11, outside this documentation repository.

x-out-of-scope-governance-envelope-field.$comment: These fields sit beside decision_payload inside one purpose packet (template.json#/purposes/<purpose>) but are excluded from the JCS/SHA-256 digest per digest_contract.governance_envelope_is_excluded. They are documented here only so a materializer cannot mistake them for decision_payload content; this schema does not validate them.

content_digest.description: sha256(JCS(decision_payload)), computed server-side after materialization. Never author-supplied. See #/$defs/sha256Hex and digest_contract in the template.

nominal_approval_record_refs.description: Six role slots (approval_record_contract.required_fields), each populated only by a recorded human/technical approval event, never by the materializer.

purpose_status.description: Driven only by the lifecycle_contract.allowed_transitions state machine, never set directly by the materializer.

controller_approved.description: Derived by eligibility_rules.human_packet_complete_requires, not fillable by the materializer.

x-forbidden-anywhere-in-this-repository.$comment: Never place these in decision_payload, in this schema's examples, or in any governance document: raw CPF/RG/passport/CNH numbers, residential address, personal phone number, personal e-mail address, bank account/card data, secrets, tokens, or full copies of civil documents. See reference doc sections 4.3, 11.2, 19.1. Use #/$defs/opaqueUuid or #/$defs/opaqueRefOrNull instead.
